Definition

The surfaces of revolution whose principal curvatures are in a constant ratio k: meridian rho = a cos^k(t). k = 1 gives the sphere, k = -1 a minimal surface (catenoid); the four sign/size regimes of k give spindles, domes, trumpets and annular waists. SHIPPED with k a live knob and the defining relation itself measured: the self-test computes the discrete meridian/parallel curvature ratio on the produced meridian and checks it equals k, converging under refinement, for k in {1, 2, -1, 0.5}; the k = 1 member is verified to be the round sphere and k = -1 exactly the catenoid rho = a cosh(z/a).
